It performs member lookup by name through class scope, qualified lookup, anonymous/derived contexts, and then delegates to build_class_member_access_expr. Since the bug manifests as access to a particular std::string internal union member, incorrect lookup/finalization of the selected member symbol is a plausible upstream source, though still less direct than constexpr union-state code.

ranked_methods.reason: Relevant upstream producer of initialization/store trees consumed by cxx_eval_store_expression. It builds INIT_EXPR/MODIFY_EXPR, routes class initialization through constructors/special member calls, and handles array/aggregate initialization and conversions. If the regression stems from changed frontend construction of the assignment/init tree for std::string internals, this method is a realistic producer of the malformed store pattern later misinterpreted by constexpr evaluation.

ranked_methods.signature: tree build_constructor (tree type, vec<constructor_elt, va_gc> *vals MEM_STAT_DECL)
ranked_methods.reason: Low-level but still plausible because the constexpr machinery models object and union state using CONSTRUCTOR nodes. This function is the canonical builder for those nodes and immediately recomputes flags. It is less likely than cp/constexpr and cp/typeck/init methods because it contains little policy, but if representation creation changed underneath constexpr union tracking, this would be on the critical path.
